title: Shadow index strategy and safe FK backfill for control-plane joins
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Several control-plane read paths (project listing, tenant lookups, and permission joins) suffer from large join times caused by sparse foreign-key columns, mixed encoding (uuid vs bigint surrogate), and bloated composite indexes. Full-table scans and repeated nested loop joins show up in p99 query traces during import and mass-tenant operations.

Goal: Introduce a low-risk, reversible approach to improve read performance and enable future schema normalization without causing downtime. The plan consists of: 1) creating 'shadow' single-column indexes and small shadow lookup tables to drive selective reads for hot joins; 2) canonically materializing surrogate FK values in a compact column via an idempotent backfill process; 3) adding planner-stable hints and metrics to verify improvement; 4) safely retiring a small set of legacy composite indexes afterwards.

Key deliverables: 
- SQL migrations to create shadow indexes and small shadow tables (idempotent, CONCURRENTLY where supported).
- A chunked backfill runner (DB job with progress table) that updates surrogate_fk_col using tenant-scoped batches and has built-in throttling and circuit-breakers.
- Read-path query rewrites that prefer shadow indexes via explicit index hints or query pattern changes, gated by a feature flag.
- Telemetry: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency dashboards, index usage counters, and backfill progress metrics.
- Rollback plan: fast revert by turning the feature flag off and dropping backfill's progress marker; indexes created CONCURRENTLY can be dropped with minimal locking.

Safety constraints: 
- All writes are unchanged; backfill writes only compact surrogate id column and is idempotent. 
- Backfill batch size default is 5k rows; configurable via runtime flag per cycle. 
- Run in canary (limited tenant cohort) for 7 days before broader rollout. 

Why this differs from previous work: Instead of heavy-handed partitioning or large composite index rewrites, this approach isolates risk by adding narrow, targeted structures that can be measured and removed without a full table rewrite. It also provides a migration path for later normalization (moving from nullable polymorphic refs to a single surrogate FK).

Important SQL examples (for reviewers): 
- Create shadow index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_shadow_project_surrogate ON project_table (surrogate_fk_col);
- Add shadow lookup table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS project_surrogate_map (raw_fk text PRIMARY KEY, surrogate_fk bigint, updated_at timestamptz);
- Backfill chunk example: UPDATE project_table SET surrogate_fk_col = m.surrogate_fk FROM (SELECT raw_fk, surrogate_fk FROM project_surrogate_map WHERE surrogate_fk IS NOT NULL LIMIT 5000) m WHERE project_table.raw_fk = m.raw_fk AND (project_table.surrogate_fk IS NULL OR project_table.surrogate_fk <> m.surrogate_fk);
comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Chen: Initial discovery notes attached. Found repeated nested loop joins on project->user mapping on high-cardinality tenants. Included sample EXPLAIN output in the PRD link.

2026-02-26 - Diego Alvarez: Pushed prototype migration and shadow index creation to staging. Verified that CONCURRENTLY works on our managed PG cluster but increases wall-clock time; adjusted default batching window.
2026-03-02 - Priya Kapoor (review): Asked for an explicit safety circuit to pause backfill if p99 increases by >25% for canary tenants. Requested test harness for idempotency verification.

2026-03-04 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented circuit-breaker and added a 'backfill_paused' boolean flag in ops config. Added integration test that runs backfill twice and asserts no duplicate or conflicting surrogate values.

2026-03-07 - Infra (review): Noted that adding several shadow indexes increases WAL churn during heavy writes. Mitigation: stagger index creation and limit concurrent maintenance windows for high-write tenants.

2026-03-10 - Performance results (staging canary, 48h): project listing p95 reduced from 420ms to 120ms for canary tenants; CPU remains within SLOs; index usage counters show 78% of reads served by shadow index after feature flag turned on.

Next steps: run a larger canary across 10% of tenants for 14 days, prepare PR for console telemetry charts, and schedule a 1-hour maintenance window to drop two legacy composite indexes if metric targets are met.
